newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-VON GRUENIGEN WINS GIANT SLALOM, AAMODT SEVENTH.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-VON GRUENIGEN WINS GIANT SLALOM, AAMODT SEVENTH.

text.p: World Cup giant slalom champion Michael von Gruenigen of Switzerland roared to victory at the World Cup Finals on Saturday, while Kjetil Andre Aamodt saw his chances for the overall title virtually vanish.

Von Gruenigen, who also won the world championship title this year, claimed his fourth victory of the World Cup season on the strength of a second run that put him nearly one second ahead of Austrian Rainer Salzgeber, the first-leg leader.
The 27-year-old Swiss, who was second by 0.18 of a second after the first run, finished with a combined time of two minutes, 18.58 seconds.
Salzgeber was second in 2:19.57, with compatriot Andreas Schifferer, winner of Thursday's Super-G, taking third place in 2:19.97, 0.31 of a second faster than Italy's Patrick Holzer.
Austrians Hermann Maier and Josef Strobl followed in fifth and sixth places ahead of Aamodt, who tied for seventh with Swede Fredrik Nyberg.
Aamodt, second best in the giant slalom standings, earned 36 points for his finish, a result that probably scuttled his chances of overtaking France's Luc Alphand for the overall title.
The Norwegian, who won the World Cup title in 1994, now trails Alphand by 70 points with only Sunday's slalom remaining to the season.

Aamodt, who ranks only eighth in the slalom standings, needs to win or finish second on Sunday to pass Alphand, who is poised to become the first Frenchman since Jean-Claude Killy in 1968 to win the overall crown.
Aamodt's best slalom finish this season was third in the season-opening slalom in Park City. In his last three slaloms, the Norwegian has finished 10th, 11th and 15th.
